summary: Attacked the extraction of Bergström–Faber–Payne, 'Polynomial point counts and odd cohomology vanishing on moduli spaces of stable curves' (Ann. of Math. 199 (2024); arXiv:2206.07759v2): 80 items, 5 routes and 6 source issues. There are ten findings: two high, five medium and three low. The numbers hold. Theorems 1.4, 1.5 and 9.6, the equivariant Theorem 11.1 and, newly checked, Theorem 11.5's local-system traces against Theorem 11.1 are all consistent. E1–E6 and the library citations hold. High findings. (1) The moduli stacks M̄_{g,n} and the Boggi–Pikaart cover are routed to MotivicStructuresInModuliOfCurves, although StableReductionPartII already owns pointed stable-curve moduli. It was accepted via PAPER-YUAN-26 and widened by the confirmed RT-AREA-etale/4, whose fix retargets CLP24 but not this extraction. (2) Display (3) of the paper omits the det E(G) orientation twist in the E₁ page of the weight spectral sequence, and the item copies it. M_{1,2} is a counterexample: χ would be 2, not 1. The paper's conclusions are unaffected; this is a new source issue. Medium findings: Poincaré duality for DM stacks has two owners (SF.2 via CLP24, WC.2 here); the squarefree count duplicates the ArithmeticStatistics ST.4 node; deligne-purity cites the consumer WC.3 instead of WC.6/DWP.7 and omits the DM-stack case; items are missing for the weight theory behind Arbarello–Cornalba's Lemma 2.6 and for symmetric functions and plethysm. Low findings: Lang's theorem, the groupoid mass shared with YU-23, and the hyperelliptic model and its point count.
checked: The source. On 29 September 2026 I re-fetched arXiv:2206.07759v2 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.07759v2, SHA-256 36beb2d3eccb42161a0b6190a653b060337f08fed5866f6b578888d503346758), which matches the record. I also fetched v1 (SHA-256 1645de99b33c6fd1a954432ebb4bb1acff1c723c0d3773ec591b4497d54ce4a9). The arXiv listing shows v2 (17 October 2023) as the last version. The Annals page (199 (2024) 1323–1365; received 30 June 2022, revised 22 June 2023, accepted 27 September 2023) serves no PDF: the file URL returns HTML. So findings are scoped to v2, as the extraction records. I read all 31 pages of v2 and checked p. 7 on a 300 dpi page image.

Every item against its locator: the statement, the hypotheses and the numbers. All 80 statements match v2, apart from the E₁ formula that the item weight-spectral-sequence copies from the paper (finding 2). Counts: 2 library, 6 planned and 72 missing items. Routes 1–5 carry 49 + 19 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 72 items, each missing item exactly once.

The numbers, recomputed independently in exact integer arithmetic, all consistent. Theorem 1.4 minus Theorem 1.5 minus Proposition 9.6 is 0 in every degree for n = 0–3, with χ(M_{4,n}) = 2, 2, −2, −10. Theorem 11.1: open plus the §11.3 boundary equals closed for all three Schur components of #_{S₃}M̄_{4,3}, which is palindromic about q⁶. The dimension-weighted sum of #_{S₃}M_{4,3} is Theorem 1.5, and χ_{S₃} = 2s₃ − 6s_{2,1}. §11.1 against Proposition 5.1 for g = 4. New check: Theorem 11.5 against the point counts. From Tr(F|V₁) = q⁷ + q², V₂ = 0 and V_{1,1} I rebuilt #M_{4,1} and #_{S₂}M_{4,2}, and they match Theorems 1.5 and 11.1. From V₃, V_{2,1} and V_{1,1,1} (Sym³ = V₃, S_{2,1} = V_{2,1} ⊕ V₁(−1), ∧³ = V_{1,1,1} ⊕ V₁(−1)) I rebuilt #_{S₃}M_{4,3} from the ordered-tuple counts N₁(N₁−1)(N₁−2), (N₂−N₁)N₁ and N₃−N₁ at q = 2–29. It matches Theorem 11.1 exactly. The squarefree recursion, #P₀ = q²(q−1), #P_g = (q−1)(q^{2g+2} − q^{2g}) and (4) were checked by hand, as were the orders in (6).

The proofs of §§2–10 step by step: Proposition 2.1 from Harer's vcd and [CFP12, MSS13]; the k = 7 and k = 9 base-case ranges; Proposition 3.1 with s = 9 + 2n and s = 9 + n; Propositions 4.2, 7.4 and 7.5; Examples 7.7–7.9; Proposition 8.8; Corollary 9.5; §10. The only new defect is display (3) (finding 2), and it does not affect the conclusions. The review's six verdicts on E1–E6 hold. I rechecked E1–E4 against the text, and E3 by the recomputation above.

Library citations at the pinned commits (declarations.tsv, then source). mathlib:quadraticChar (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/QuadraticChar/Basic.lean:120), mathlib:quadraticChar_sum_zero (same file, line 239, hypothesis ringChar F ≠ 2) and mathlib:Matrix.card_GL_field (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Card.lean:99) all exist and give their items. Mathlib also has Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup (…/GeneralLinearGroup/Projective.lean:41), and Tau Ceti has TauCeti.GeneralLinear.centerPointwiseQuotientIsoPGL for the PGL₄ quotient. Name searches for squarefree polynomial counts, plethysm, symmetric functions, Schur functions, moduli stacks and point counts of stacks find nothing else relevant.

Planned statuses against the stage texts and the integrated decompositions. SF.2 is the integration owner of UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting (data/atlas.json 'external'). The WC.1 nodes zeta-function-euler-product-and-point-counts and cohomological-formula-from-the-trace-formula hold for trace-formula-varieties, hasse-weil-zeta, zeta-determinant and zeta-multiplicative. WC.4 holds for etale-singular-comparison: it is the only stage that plans the dimension comparison with singular cohomology. WC.3 does not hold for deligne-purity (finding 5).

Routes and owners. I read the atlas texts of WC.0–WC.7, DWP.0–DWP.10, FF.1, FF.3, ST.5 and GN.2. I read the packets for FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums, ArithmeticStatistics, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, WC.0, WC.6 and DWP.0. The Tau Ceti documents read were StableReduction (Layers 1–3 and its 'Boundary' section), HodgeStructures L2, SchurWeyl L7, InductionRestriction L6 and AlgebraicCurves L10.
- I searched every paper extraction's routes for curve/moduli/point-count roadmaps, and every item for stack point counts, equivariant counts, the sieve and inverse zeta, polynomial counts, squarefree counts, Lang's theorem, Poincaré duality for DM stacks and quadrics over F_q.
- I read PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 (route 1 brief and items 1–93), PAPER-YUAN-26 and PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 (StableReductionPartII), RT-AREA-etale.fixes.md finding /4, RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry.md (its note on the M_{g,n} owners), and the queue states of the DESIGN, BP and RT jobs involved.
- Routes 3 (DWP.8; the weight spectral sequence is planned nowhere else) and 5 (GN.2) hold.
- Route 2's WC.5:power-sum-converse note ('in bound form') is accurate.

The review's changes. It changed only the six E-verdicts and the report. Its claim that vdBE Lemma 4.1 is 'exactly WC.5:power-sum-converse' overstates the match: the lemma also needs the weights of the eigenvalues. The item's own note is accurate, so I raise no finding.

Self-interest disclosure. This session wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-74 and PAPER-DELIGNE-80. Finding 5 cites PAPER-DELIGNE-80's planned statuses for Weil II (3.3.9) and (3.3.11). No other finding concerns their routes or items.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24.result.json: item PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/weight-spectral-sequence (statement), item PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/moduli-stacks (as used for E₁), sourceIssues (no entry); source: arXiv:2206.07759v2, proof of Proposition 4.2, display (3), p. 7
findings.claim: Display (3) gives the E₁ page of the weight spectral sequence for H^•_c(M_{g,n}) as E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} H^k(M̃_G), with H^•(M̃_G) = (⊗_v H^•(M̄_{g_v,n_v}))^{Aut(G)}. That is false: the correct term carries the orientation local system ε^j of the j boundary branches, so E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} (H^k(∏_v M̄_{g_v,n_v}) ⊗ det E(G))^{Aut(G)}. The paper's own citation [PW21, §2.3] states the twisted form. The item weight-spectral-sequence copies the untwisted formula, and neither the extraction nor the review records it. Counterexample (g, n) = (1, 2). Two graphs have |E| = 2: (c) two genus-0 vertices, each with one leg, joined by two edges, with Aut(G) = Z/2 swapping the edges; and (d) a genus-0 vertex with a loop joined to a genus-0 vertex carrying both legs, with Aut(G) = Z/2 flipping the loop. Both vertex products are points. In (c) the swap acts by −1 on det E(G), so its twisted invariants vanish, while its untwisted invariants are Q. All k are even. Row j = 0 is H^•(M̄_{1,2}) with Betti numbers 1, 2, 1. Row j = 1 has the two graphs M̄_{0,4}/(Z/2) and M̄_{1,1} × M̄_{0,3}, each contributing 1 + 1. So the Euler characteristic of the abutment is 4 − 4 + 1 = 1 with the twist and 4 − 4 + 2 = 2 without it. But #M_{1,2}(F_q) = q², since #M_{1,2} = Σ_E (#E(F_q) − 1)/#Aut(E) = q·#M_{1,1} − Σ_E a_E/#Aut(E) = q², where the a_E-sum vanishes by quadratic twisting as in Lemma 5.2. So χ_c(M_{1,2}) = 1, and the untwisted (3) is wrong. The paper's conclusions survive. Proposition 4.2 and Corollary 9.5 use only that each E₁ row is built from H^•(M̄_{g_v,n_v}) by finite-group invariants, with Frobenius eigenvalues p^k and dimensions independent of p. Twisting by the sign character det E(G), on which Frobenius acts trivially because the branches are defined over Z, changes neither. The same paragraph also says the spectral sequence 'abuts to the compactly supported cohomology of M_{g,n}' in a proof about M_{g′,n′}.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2206.07759v2 p. 7 (page image at 300 dpi checked): 'H^•(M̃_G) = (⊗_{v∈V(G)} H^•(M̄_{g_v,n_v}))^{Aut(G)}. The weight spectral sequence abuts to the compactly supported cohomology of M_{g,n}, collapses at E₂, and has E₁-page given by (3) E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} H^k(M̃_G).' Payne–Willwacher, arXiv:2110.05711v1 (SHA-256 8cd8404c6bad611eae16c458748ce4847f586efd4e129f9aaa7603f4695f3a84), §2.3, p. 5: 'The monodromy action on these branches defines a local system of rank j on D̃^j whose determinant is denoted ε^j. The E₁-page … E₁^{j,k} ≅ H^k(D̃^j, ε^j) … the local system ε^j is identified with the determinant of the permutation action of Aut(Γ) on E(Γ). Thus, we have E₁^{j,k} ≅ ⊕_{|E(Γ)|=j} (H^k(M̄_Γ) ⊗ det E(Γ))^{Aut(Γ)}.' PAPER-CANNING-LARSON-PAYNE-24 item /87 also writes the twist ('(H^{15}(M̄_Γ) ⊗ det E(Γ))^{Aut(Γ)}'). The (1, 2) computation is given in the claim; #M̄_{1,2}(F_q) = q² + 2q + 1 and #M_{1,2}(F_q) = q² are Getzler's genus-one counts [Get98], which the paper cites for g = 1, n ≤ 10.
findings.fix: (1) Restate item weight-spectral-sequence: 'E₁^{j,k} = ⊕_{|E(G)|=j} (H^k(∏_{v} M̄_{g_v,n_v}) ⊗ det E(G))^{Aut(G)} = H^k(D̃^{(j)}, ε^j), where D̃^{(j)} = ⊔_{|E(G)|=j} M̃_G and ε^j is the determinant of the local system of the j boundary branches; the sequence abuts to H^{j+k}_c(M_{g,n}) and degenerates at E₂ (Payne–Willwacher §2.3; Deligne, Hodge II §3.2, dual form)'. Add to its note: 'The paper's (3) omits det E(G) (sourceIssues E7).' (2) Add sourceIssues entry PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24/E7: kind 'error'; locator 'proof of Proposition 4.2, display (3), p. 7 (arXiv v2)'; printed as quoted; correction as in (1), and 'M_{g,n}' should read 'M_{g′,n′}' in the preceding sentence; reason: the M_{1,2} Euler-characteristic counterexample; affects 'nothing' (Propositions 4.2 and 9.5 hold, since the sign twist changes neither Frobenius eigenvalues nor p-independence of dimensions); known 'new; the cited [PW21, §2.3] states the twisted formula'; searched: the arXiv listing (v2 is the last version), Crossref (no update relation) and the Annals page (no erratum listed); the Annals text is not openly available and was not collated. (3) Add to the DWP.8 route reason that the E₁ term carries the orientation local system, and to the moduli-roadmap brief that every graph sum over boundary strata is taken with det E(G).

findings.claim: The planned owner is wrong, and the generality the paper needs is not stated. WC.3 is a consumer of purity for smooth projective varieties ('Import DWP.4's proved purity'), whereas the item states purity for smooth proper varieties. That case is planned by the integrated decomposition node WeilConjectures:WC.6/purity-for-proper-smooth-varieties (Weil II 3.3.9) and by DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.7 (node …/hodge-type-triangles-and-proper-smooth-purity-3-3-7-3-3-11). The paper applies purity to smooth proper DM stacks: in Proposition 3.1 the α_{i,j} on H^i(M̄_{4,n}) must have weight i for vdBE Lemma 4.1, and Proposition 4.2 needs the same. For a DM stack this follows either from Weil II (3.3.11), since the coarse space has quotient singularities and so is a rational homology manifold, or from the Boggi–Pikaart global quotient and invariants. The same DWP.7 node plans 3.3.11. No item states the DM-stack case or names this route. Disclosure: this red team (cc-f805bf) wrote PAPER-DELIGNE-80, which lists (3.3.9) as planned at DWP.7, WC.6 and WC.3, and (3.3.11) as planned at DWP.7 and EDC.1. This finding cites those items as evidence of where the theorems are planned.

findings.claim: Arbarello–Cornalba's Lemma 2.6, the injection H^k(M̄_{g,n}) ↪ H^k of the normalized boundary, uses 'a bit of Hodge theory', and the extraction has no item for it. The input is: (i) H^k of a smooth proper DM stack is pure of weight k; (ii) for a proper variety or DM stack Y and a proper surjection Ỹ → Y from a smooth proper source (here the normalization of the normal-crossings boundary), the kernel of H^k(Y) → H^k(Ỹ) is W_{k−1}H^k(Y), and H^k(Y) has weights ≤ k (Deligne, Hodge III, 8.2.5; ℓ-adically Weil II 3.3.1 with cohomological descent). The pure-Tate claim of §1 also needs the mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of the coarse space. In the atlas, Tau Ceti HodgeStructures L2 plans mixed Hodge structures only as linear algebra (filtrations and the Deligne splitting). No stage plans Deligne's mixed Hodge structure on the cohomology of a variety or DM stack. DWP.7 plans the ℓ-adic weight bound, but not the kernel statement (ii). Both items are routed as moduli-specific ('Weight-filtration argument'), which hides general inputs.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2206.07759v2 §2, p. 4: 'Using “a bit of Hodge theory,” i.e., basic properties of Deligne's weight filtration, Arbarello and Cornalba improve this statement as follows. Lemma ([AC98, Lemma 2.6]). Suppose H^k_c(M_{g,n}) = 0. Then pullback to the normalization of the boundary gives an injection H^k(M̄_{g,n}) ↪ H^k(∂̃M̄_{g,n}).' Item ac-lemma-2-6 note: 'Weight-filtration argument; routed to the moduli-of-curves roadmap.' Stage text of tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures#milestone-l2--mixed-hodge-structures-strictness-deligne (content/tau-ceti/HodgeStructures/README.md, L2): definitions of MixedHodgeStructure V, strictness and the Deligne splitting, with no cohomology of varieties. A regex search of all 1968 atlas stage descriptions for 'mixed Hodge structure on (the) cohomology', 'Hodge II/III' and 'Théorie de Hodge' finds only HodgeStructures L2 and R09.7/R09.7d (a citation of Hodge II 4.4.3 for Borel extension).
findings.fix: Add an item weights-of-proper-varieties: 'For Y proper over F_q (resp. C), H^k(Y) is mixed of weights ≤ k, and for a proper surjective Ỹ → Y with Ỹ smooth proper, ker(H^k(Y) → H^k(Ỹ)) = W_{k−1}H^k(Y) (Hodge III 8.2.5; Weil II 3.3.1 with cohomological descent); for a smooth proper DM stack H^k is pure of weight k.' Set its status to planned at DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7 for the ℓ-adic weight bound. Route the kernel statement as a source to DWP.7, or, for the Hodge realisation, record it as missing in the route 1 brief with an import note. Make ac-lemma-2-6 and pure-tate cite it. Add to route 1's brief: 'import the weight theory of the cohomology of proper varieties and DM stacks (DWP.7; Hodge-theoretic realisation from its owner, with the linear algebra of Tau Ceti HodgeStructures L2)'.

findings.claim: §§9 and 11 compute in the ring of symmetric functions, and nothing in the extraction plans it. The inputs are: the representation ring R(G) (Definition 9.1 values #_G X(F_q) in it); the identification of irreducible S_n-representations with Schur functions s_λ (the Frobenius characteristic); power sums p_n and plethysm, with p_n ∘ q = q^n; and the Exp/Log of stable S-modules in the Getzler–Kapranov formula Ch(MV) = Log(exp(Δ) Exp(Ch V)). Part of this is planned upstream. Tau Ceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction Layer 6 plans R(G) and its character map. RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl Layer 7 plans the Frobenius characteristic, but only in a finite-variable, degree-bounded form, and defers 'the stable symmetric-function ring and the Hall inner product'. Plethysm, the stable ring and Exp/Log are planned nowhere. The GSp(8) highest-weight representations behind V_λ (local-systems) are planned in RepresentationTheory ClassicalGroups/LieHighestWeight, which the item does not cite.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2206.07759v2 §9.2, p. 22: 'Definition 9.1. The G-equivariant point count #_G X(F_q) is the element of the representation ring of G associated to the class function σ ↦ #X^σ(F_q)'; p. 23: 'writing s_λ for the Schur function that corresponds to the character of the irreducible representation V_λ'; proof of Proposition 9.6, p. 23: 'noting that p_n ∘ q = q^n, where p_n is the degree n power sum symmetric function and ∘ denotes plethysm'. Stage text tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SchurWeyl#layer-7-symmetric-functions-the-frobenius-characteristic-and-rsk: 'The stable symmetric-function ring and the Hall inner product … are deferred to a later, separately stated step'. Stage text …/InductionRestriction#layer-6-the-virtual-character-ring-artin-and-brauer-induction: 'The representation ring and its character map. The primary object is the Grothendieck ring R(G) of FDRep k G'. A regex search of all atlas stages for 'plethysm' finds nothing.
findings.fix: Add three items. (a) representation-ring: planned at tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction#layer-6-the-virtual-character-ring-artin-and-brauer-induction. (b) frobenius-characteristic (irreducible V_λ ↔ s_λ, power sums): planned at …/SchurWeyl#layer-7-symmetric-functions-the-frobenius-characteristic-and-rsk for fixed n; the stable ring over all n is missing. (c) plethysm-and-exp-log (the λ-ring of symmetric functions, plethysm, p_n ∘ q = q^n, Exp and Log of stable S-modules): missing. Route (b)'s stable part and (c) with route 1, and add to its brief: 'import R(G) and the Frobenius characteristic from Tau Ceti InductionRestriction L6 and SchurWeyl L7; the stable symmetric-function ring, plethysm and Exp/Log are planned here, before the Getzler–Kapranov layer, unless the maintainer opens a SchurWeyl Part II for them'. Cite RepresentationTheory ClassicalGroups/LieHighestWeight in local-systems for the GSp(8) representations.

findings.claim: Proposition 1.3(ii) rests on Lang's theorem (every torsor under a connected linear algebraic group over F_q is trivial). The note names it, but it has no item or owner. The accepted PAPER-LIPNOWSKI-TSIMERMAN-18 routes 'Lang's theorem over finite fields' (item lang-theorem) to ReductiveGroupsPartII (route 13, accepted).

findings.claim: Lemma 5.2's proof uses two standard facts that are not items. First, the model C_f of a hyperelliptic curve as the closure of y² = f(x) in P(1, 1, g+1), for f squarefree of degree 2g+1 or 2g+2 and q odd. Tau Ceti AlgebraicCurves Layer 10 plans this ('char ≠ 2 models y² = f(x), f squarefree of degree 2g+1 or 2g+2, with the converse genus formula'). Second, the point count #C_f(F_q) = q + 1 + Σ_{x ∈ P¹(F_q)} χ(f(x)), with evaluation at ∞ through the leading coefficient. The FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums packet plans this only for elliptic curves (FF.3/point-count-as-character-sum).
findings.evidence: arXiv:2206.07759v2 proof of Lemma 5.2, p. 8: 'Let C_f be the closure in P(1, 1, g + 1) of the affine curve given by y² = f(x), for f ∈ P_g. Since q is odd, every hyperelliptic curve is of this form.' The next display uses (q + 1 − #C(F_q))² = (Σ_{x∈P¹(F_q)} χ(f(x)))². Stage text tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-10-model-classes--elliptic-hyperelliptic-plane-curves. Packet node FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.3/point-count-as-character-sum: 'For q odd and W with a₁ = a₃ = 0: naivePointCount W = q + 1 + Σ_{x∈F} χ(f(x))'.
findings.fix: Add item hyperelliptic-model-count: 'for q odd and f ∈ P_g, C_f ⊂ P(1,1,g+1) is a smooth hyperelliptic curve of genus g, every hyperelliptic curve over F_q has this form, and #C_f(F_q) = q + 1 + Σ_{x∈P¹(F_q)} χ(f(x))'. Mark the model planned at tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves#layer-10-model-classes--elliptic-hyperelliptic-plane-curves. Route the count as a source to FiniteFieldsAndCharacterSums:FF.3, next to its elliptic node.
